unit_description: This unit develops flexible subtraction strategies. Students subtract three-digit numbers on a number line, use expanded form and compensation, and solve word problems without regrouping.
unit_goals: Subtract three-digit numbers on a number line.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students explore number-line, expanded-form, and compensation subtraction strategies, and apply them to word problems without regrouping.

lessons.lesson_title: Subtract Three-Digit Numbers on a Number Line
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by subtracting multiples of ten on a number line.
lessons.concept: Subtraction on a number line means jumping left. Start at the whole, then jump back the subtrahend in friendly pieces.
lessons.practice: Subtract three-digit numbers by making jumps of hundreds, tens, and ones on a number line.
lessons.objective: Subtract three-digit numbers using a number line.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by subtracting tens mentally.

learn.title: Subtract Three-Digit Numbers on a Number Line
teaching_points: Start at the whole (the bigger number).
Jump back by hundreds, then tens, then ones.
Where you land is the difference.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Solve each subtraction problem by making jumps on the number line.

flashcards.title: Subtraction Vocabulary
flashcards.instructions: Review subtraction words and number-line moves.

bigIdea.title: Subtract Three-Digit Numbers on a Number Line
bigIdea.subtitle: Jump back to find the difference
bigIdea.intro: A number line helps you subtract by breaking the number you are taking away into friendly jumps. Jump back by hundreds, tens, and ones.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why are friendly jumps helpful when subtracting?

ruleCards.description: Place your starting point at the larger number.
Break the subtrahend into hundreds, tens, and ones.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by subtracting the hundreds, tens, and ones separately.
lessons.concept: Expanded form breaks each number into its place values. Subtract hundreds from hundreds, tens from tens, and ones from ones, then put the number back together.
lessons.practice: Subtract two three-digit numbers using expanded form.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by subtracting matching place values.

learn.title: Subtract Using Expanded Form
teaching_points: Break each number into hundreds, tens, and ones.
Combine the place values to find the difference.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Subtract each pair of numbers using expanded form.

bigIdea.title: Subtract Using Expanded Form
bigIdea.subtitle: Subtract each place value separately
bigIdea.intro: Expanded form breaks numbers into their parts. When you subtract matching places, you can see why the digits line up.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why do the place values have to line up?

ruleCards.description: Write each number as the sum of its place values.
Subtract matching places, then combine them into one number.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by subtracting multiples of ten and one near a hundred.
lessons.concept: Compensation means changing both numbers by the same amount to make the subtraction easier. The difference stays the same.
lessons.practice: Subtract by adjusting both numbers to create a friendly problem.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by making subtraction friendly.

questions.hint: 15 - 10 = 5, but you took away one too many, so add 1 back.
250 - 100 = 150, plus 3 because you took 3 too many.

learn.title: Subtract Using Compensation
teaching_points: Change both numbers by the same amount.
Make the subtrahend a friendly number.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Use compensation to make each subtraction problem easier.

flashcards.title: Compensation Moves
flashcards.instructions: Review how to use compensation in subtraction.

bigIdea.title: Subtract Using Compensation
bigIdea.subtitle: Adjust both numbers by the same amount
bigIdea.intro: When the number you are subtracting is close to a friendly number, add the same small amount to both numbers. The difference stays the same.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why does the difference stay the same when you compensate?

ruleCards.description: Add the same amount to both numbers so the second becomes friendly.
The distance between the two numbers does not change.

lessons.lesson_title: Subtract Without Regrouping and Solve Word Problems
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up with three no-regrouping subtraction facts.
lessons.concept: When each digit in the top number is greater than or equal to the digit below it, subtract each column without regrouping. Use this in word problems to find differences.
lessons.practice: Subtract without regrouping and solve one-step subtraction word problems.
lessons.objective: Subtract without regrouping and solve word problems.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by subtracting without regrouping.

questions.hint: Subtract ones, then tens, then hundreds.

questions.prompt: A store had 348 shirts and sold 125. How many are left?

learn.title: Subtract Without Regrouping
teaching_points: Subtract the ones, then the tens, then the hundreds.
If the top digit in each place is larger, no regrouping is needed.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A library has 489 books checked out. After returns, 167 fewer are checked out. How many are still checked out?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Subtract each pair of numbers or solve the word problem. No regrouping needed.

flashcards.title: No-Regrouping Subtraction
flashcards.instructions: Review no-regrouping subtraction and key words.

bigIdea.title: Subtract Without Regrouping and Solve Word Problems
bigIdea.subtitle: Subtract each column separately
bigIdea.intro: When the top digit in each place is at least as large as the bottom digit, you can subtract straight down. This helps you solve how-many-more or how-many-left word problems.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do you know if you need to regroup?

ruleCards.description: Make sure ones are under ones, tens under tens, and hundreds under hundreds.
If the top digit in every column is larger or equal, you do not need to regroup.

lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of number-line, expanded-form, compensation, and no-regrouping subtraction.
lessons.concept: Review the four subtraction strategies from this unit: number line, expanded form, compensation, and no-regrouping subtraction.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about subtraction strategies.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: number line + expanded form + compensation + no regrouping = subtraction strategies

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Which is the best estimate for 602 - 298?

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 6 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 6 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Subtraction Strategies
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: number-line subtraction, expanded-form subtraction, compensation, and no-regrouping subtraction.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about subtraction strategies?

ruleCards.description: You can use any strategy that makes the problem easy for you.
When the top digit in each place is larger, subtract each column separately.
